claims.claim: In January 1977 the Senate Select Committee on Nutrition and Human Needs (the McGovern committee) issued the Dietary Goals for the United States.
claims.episode_span: the 1977 Dietary Goals for the United States, drafted by the Senate Select Committee on Nutrition and Human Needs under Senator George McGovern
claims.source_title: United States Senate Select Committee on Nutrition and Human Needs - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: In January 1977, after having held hearings on the national diet, the McGovern committee issued a new set of nutritional guidelines for Americans

claims.claim: The 1977 Dietary Goals recommended reducing fat to 30 percent of energy intake and saturated fat to 10 percent.
claims.episode_span: recommended that Americans reduce total fat to 30 percent of calories and saturated fat to 10 percent
claims.supporting_quote: reducing fat from 40% to 30% of energy intake, reducing eating saturated fat to 10% of energy intake, reducing cholesterol consumption to 300 milligrams daily

claims.claim: The first Dietary Guidelines for Americans were released in 1980 and have been revised every five years.
claims.episode_span: The 1980 Dietary Guidelines for Americans and subsequent editions carried the same emphasis
claims.supporting_quote: First released in 1980, the guidelines have been revised every five years, with the 10th edition released in January 2026.

claims.claim: Ancel Keys hypothesized that dietary saturated fat contributed to cardiovascular disease.
claims.episode_span: the prevailing hypothesis, advanced by Ancel Keys and others, that dietary fat and especially saturated fat raised serum cholesterol
claims.supporting_quote: In particular, he hypothesized that replacing dietary saturated fat with polyunsaturated fat reduced cardiovascular diseases

claims.claim: The USDA's 1992 Food Guide Pyramid placed 6 to 11 servings of bread, cereal, rice and pasta at its base.
claims.episode_span: In 1992 the USDA unveiled its Food Guide Pyramid with a broad base of 6 to 11 daily servings of bread, cereal, rice, and pasta
claims.source_title: History of USDA nutrition guidelines - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: The introduction of the USDA's food guide pyramid in 1992 attempted to express the recommended servings of each food group, which previous guides did not do. 6 to 11 servings of bread, cereal, rice and pasta occupied the large base of the pyramid

claims.claim: The 2005 MyPyramid revision added a figure climbing stairs to represent exercise.
claims.episode_span: The 2005 revision added an exercise figure and distinguished whole grains
claims.source_title: History of USDA nutrition guidelines - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: Stairs were added up the left side of the pyramid with an image of a climber to represent a push for exercise.

claims.claim: MyPlate replaced the USDA pyramid diagram on June 2, 2011, ending 19 years of food-pyramid iconography.
claims.episode_span: In 2011 the USDA replaced the pyramid entirely with MyPlate
claims.source_title: History of USDA nutrition guidelines - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: It replaced the USDA's MyPyramid diagram on June 2, 2011, ending 19 years of food pyramid iconography.

claims.claim: NHANES data show US adult obesity prevalence rose by roughly 16 percentage points between 1976-1980 and 1999-2000.
claims.episode_span: adult obesity prevalence rising from 15 percent in 1976–1980 to 31 percent by 1999–2002
claims.source_title: Obesity in the United States - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: The prevalence of obesity for adults aged 20 to 74 years increased by 7.9 percentage points for men and by 8.9 percentage points for women between 1976–1980 and 1988–1994, and subsequently by 7.1 percentage points for men and by 8.1 percentage points for women between 1988–1994 and 1999–2000.
